deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT. The previous page traces rays trigonometrically through an objective. It gives intersection distances of about 282.8 for apertures 0, 0.072 and 0.102. This page is a third-order (thin-lens) shortcut for choosing the third radius r'' of the system, positive when convex toward the object. The radius should remove the residual colour error and the residual spherical error left by the preceding surfaces. The shortcut is then tested against an exactly computed value.

DATA AND NOTATION (from the page).
- a = image distance of mean-colour axial rays.
- a−p = image distance of violet axial rays, so p is the residual longitudinal colour error.
- a−q = image distance of mean-colour marginal rays, so q is the residual longitudinal spherical aberration.
- n = mean refractive index of the glass; n+ζ = violet index, so ζ is the dispersion.
- φ = angle of the marginal ray.
- t = p/(aζ) is a dimensionless measure of the power needed to cancel the colour error p.

FORMULA. The page gives
1/r'' = A/a − B t/a ± (1/a) sqrt( C qζ/(p tan²φ) + D − E t − F t² ),
with
- A = 2(n+1)/(n+2)
- B = n(2n+1)/(2(n+2))
- C = 2n/((n−1)(n+2))
- D = n²/(n+2)²
- E = n²(n−1)/(n+2)²
- F = n²(4n−1)/(4(n+2)²)

Why a quadratic (my interpretation, not derivable from the page alone): the colour condition is linear in the curvatures and fixes the lens power, which is the role of t. Third-order spherical aberration is quadratic in the bending. Eliminating the power leaves a quadratic in 1/r''; completing the square gives the ± root.

COEFFICIENTS. From A = 1.4447145 one gets n = (2A−2)/(2−A) ≈ 1.60175; the next page uses n−1 = 0.60177. Values given: A = 1.4447145; log B = 9.9706694; log C = 0.1696837; D = 0.1977736 (log 9.2961684); log E = 9.0755989; log F = 9.4270712 (an earlier value 9.1652656 is struck out). All agree with the formulas at n ≈ 1.6018: B = 0.93469, C = 1.47803, D = 0.19777, E = 0.11901, F = 0.26734.

EXAMPLE. a = 97.446, 2p = 4.17055, 2ζ = 0.03992, q = 1.90260, φ = 6°18′32″.
- Logarithms: log 2p = 0.62019. The arithmetic complement of log 2ζ is 1.39881; the struck '1.79881' is a slip. The complement of log a is 8.01124.
- Sum: log t = 0.03024, so t = 1.07211.

First trial (later abandoned). It used log t = 0.02024, a slip of 0.01, so t = 1.0477.
- Bt = 0.97928, giving A − Bt = 0.46543.
- Radicand: the C-term came out as 2.25347 (too large by the factor 10^0.01, the same slip). Adding D = 0.19777, −Et = −0.12469 and −Ft² = −0.29346 gives 2.03309.
- sqrt = 1.42587 (log 1.89130 = 0.27676).
- log r'' = 1.98876 − 0.27676 = 1.71200, so r'' = 51.522. Gauss marks it 's.s.' (soll sein, 'should be') 1.71829, i.e. 52.274.

Second computation, with t = 1.07211.
- A − Bt = 1.44471 − 1.00209 = 0.44262.
- Radicand: C qζ/(p tan²φ) = 2.20216 (checks: qζ/p = 0.018211, tan²φ = 0.012223). Then +0.19777, −0.10135, −0.30729; Ft² = 0.30729 is correct.
- sqrt ≈ 1.41117; sum 1.85379, log 0.26806.
- log r'' = 1.72070, so r'' = 52.565.
- Against s.s. 1.71819 / 52.274 he records 'Corr.' −251 (units of the 5th log decimal) and −0.291.

Second example. t: log 0.03126. Approximate log 1.68533 (r'' = 48.454) against exact 1.68068 (47.939). Corrections −445 and −0.515.

PURPOSE. This is a calibration of the third-order closed formula against exact trigonometric ray tracing. Gauss then applies empirical corrections, in log and in length, to the approximate radius.
errors: In the abandoned first trial log t was taken as 0.02024 instead of 0.03024. This inflated the C-term (2.25347 instead of 2.20216) and altered Bt, Et and Ft². Gauss noticed it and recomputed.

In the second computation −Et is written −0.10135. With log E = 9.0755989 and t = 1.07211 the value should be E·t = 0.12760. The written value corresponds to log 9.00584, i.e. the log taken 0.1 too small. Ft² = 0.30729 is correct. With the corrected Et the radicand is about 1.96504, giving r'' ≈ 52.13 instead of 52.565. Probable slip, unless the intended E differs from the written formula.

The two 's.s.' log values disagree: 1.71829 (first trial) vs 1.71819 (second). Since log 52.274 = 1.71829, the 1.71819 is the slip. The correction should therefore be −241, not −251; the length correction −0.291 is right.
Second example: 1.68533 − 1.68068 = 0.00465, but −445 is written. The length difference 0.515 is correct (possible misreading of 465).

results.what: Closed approximate formula, a quadratic solved with ± root, for one radius of an objective that removes given residual longitudinal colour (p) and spherical (q) aberration. The coefficients A..F are rational functions of n.
results.modern_name: Thin-lens third-order (Seidel-type) aberration design of an achromatic, spherically corrected objective; bending equation solved as a quadratic
results.usually_credited_to: 18th–19th c. dioptrics: Euler, Clairaut, d'Alembert, J. Herschel (1821); Gauss himself published 'Über die achromatischen Doppelobjective' (1817)

results.what: Checking the approximate formula against exact trigonometric ray tracing and deriving empirical corrections (Corr. −251 / −0.291, −445 / −0.515).
results.modern_name: Validation of a third-order design against exact ray trace (higher-order residual)
results.usually_credited_to: Standard practice of optical computation (Fraunhofer, Gauss, Seidel, Steinheil)

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine third-order objective design, consistent with Gauss's known 1817 work on achromatic double objectives and his Dioptrik papers. The value of the page is as a worked numerical calibration, not a new result.

checkable.asserts: r'' ≈ 52.56 as computed on the page

transcription_corrections: 'C2ζ .... 1.79881' (struck) and 'Ca .... 8.01124': 'C' means arithmetic complement of the logarithm. The correct complement of log 2ζ is 1.39881.
The struck '29262' beside t is probably the erroneous first value of log t (0.02024); uncertain.
'98876' and '26806' in the lower column are log mantissas: log a = 1.98876 and log 1.85379 = 0.26806.
The faint overwriting above A in the main formula (apparently '(n+1)') belongs to an earlier version of the numerator.
